title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff <= Limit
statement: Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray in which the difference between its largest and smallest element is at most limit.

hints.1_question: Inside a window you need its current max and min quickly. What structure keeps the max (and min) available while elements enter and leave?
hints.2_nudge: Use two monotonic deques over the window: one decreasing (front is max), one increasing (front is min). Shrink the window while max - min > limit.
hints.3_big_hint: For each right: update both deques. While nums[mx[0]] - nums[mn[0]] > limit: left += 1 and pop any deque front whose index < left. Track right - left + 1.

known_bugs.name: forgets to pop deque fronts that left the window
known_bugs.followup: When left moves forward, is the front of each deque guaranteed to still be inside the window?

known_bugs.name: length computed as right - left
known_bugs.followup: How long is a window where left == right?

known_bugs.name: recomputes max() and min() of the window each time
known_bugs.followup: How many elements do max() and min() scan each step when the window is large? What could hand you the max and min in O(1)?

followups: Why do you need two deques rather than one?
Why does a sorted container (tree map) solution cost O(n log n) here?
